- When sentiment shows strong positive momentum (e.g., >0.67 over recent days) and news volume is high, model tends to overestimate prices — apply downward bias correction.
- If sentiment shifts sharply upward from negative to positive (e.g., +1.00+ in 1–2 days), model often overshoots — reduce forecast by 5–10% in next 3–5 days.
- When sentiment is neutral or declining (e.g., <0.33 or negative change), model frequently underestimates — add 3–7% upward bias to compensate.
- If model forecast spikes >10% above recent 7-day average, check sentiment change — if sentiment is flat or negative, reduce forecast by 10–20% to avoid overreaction.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome exceeds model by >5% for 3+ consecutive days, apply mean reversion rule: next forecast = previous + 0.5×(true - model) to avoid sustained overestimation.
- If news volume drops to 0 for 2+ days, model tends to lag — forecast should be adjusted upward by 2–5% to reflect delayed market reaction.
